beginner.headline: Pilot Saves Lives During Attack
beginner.brief: Capt Smit Machchhar was the pilot of a Flydubai plane. His co-pilot attacked him in the cockpit during the flight. Captain Machchhar opened the door to let other people in. He did not want others to die on the plane. The plane fell more than 17,000 feet during the attack. Other passengers helped to stop the attacker. Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely. Many people now praise Captain Machchhar for his courage.

intermediate.headline: Pilot's Heroism on Flydubai Flight During Co-pilot Attack
intermediate.brief: Capt Smit Machchhar, an Indian pilot, was stabbed by his co-pilot during a Flydubai flight. Despite his injuries, Machchhar was determined not to let others die and opened the cockpit door for help. He realized the plane, carrying over 170 passengers, was sinking and knew he had to act. Flydubai's flight FZ1073, bound for Tel Aviv from Dubai, plunged over 17,000 feet during its journey. The plane sent an emergency signal to air traffic controllers, then switched to a code indicating hijacking. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reported that one pilot stabbed the other, apparently trying to crash the plane. After passengers overpowered the attacker, two reserve pilots onboard safely landed the plane in Saudi Arabia. Machchhar, hailed as a "true hero" by Netanyahu, is now recovering in a stable condition in Abu Dhabi. Machchhar said he views his wound "as a journey which is slowly going on and will take time." He is confident that his recovery will happen and he will become fit and healthy again.

advanced.headline: Pilot's Heroism on Flydubai Flight After Co-Pilot Attack
advanced.brief: The Indian pilot of the Flydubai plane, who was stabbed by his co-pilot and opened the cockpit door to let others in, has said he was determined not to let others die. Capt Smit Machchhar said he was on the floor and still being attacked when he realised the plane carrying more than 170 passengers was sinking and he had to do something. "I was lying on the floor injured but I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside," he said in a video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Others came in and also played a role in controlling the situation. Flydubai's flight FZ1073, bound for Tel Aviv from Dubai, plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey. It first sent an emergency signal to air traffic controllers before switching to code squawk 7500, which indicates hijacking. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later told the media that one pilot had stabbed the other before "apparently trying to crash" the plane. After fellow passengers overpowered the attacker, two reserve pilots, who were onboard, safely landed the plane at Tabuk Airport in north-western Saudi Arabia. Machchhar, who has been hailed as a "true hero" by Netanyahu, was taken to hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition. Netanyahu told Fox News the attacker was an Omani national and said investigations suggested he had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination". He said that once the attacker had been subdued and tied up by passengers and crew, he was "calling out to the aircrew 'kill me, kill me', so it's clear he was suicidal - that's not a question". The United Arab Emirates has begun investigating "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose", according to the country's state news agency. Indian social media has been awash with praise for Machchhar since his identity emerged. The Indian Prime Minister told him that "his courage, patience and quick decision-making saved the lives of so many people" and the whole country was proud of him. The Indian embassy in the UAE said Machchhar was "in good health and recovering well". "I am not looking at this wound like a wound because that would make my recovery even more difficult," Machchhar said.
